entries.title: Live working, retry and compaction indicators with countdown disposal
entries.what: Displays working facts and operation-specific status labels, updates retry countdowns, and disposes replaced timers while preserving compaction visibility.
entries.mechanism:
StatusIndicator extends the terminal Loader, carries kind working/retry/compaction/branchSummary and disposes by stopping it. Working uses render-time detail callbacks; retry owns an additional countdown, while compaction and branch summary supply distinct reason-specific messages.

WorkingStatusIndicator keeps a mutable appearance holder so constructor-captured color functions observe later appearance updates without recreating its Loader timer. Spinner color uses indicator.color with label styles; label uses label presentation. setAppearance changes colors only in this subclass, not the frame cadence; frames are supplied separately by the host's effective working indicator. With details and at least2 Loader rows, it appends elapsed time, positive output-token count (optional '~'), reasoning level except off, and a current app.interrupt hint unless interruptible=false. It clips the resulting second row and optional gutter detail to width. formatElapsed clamps negative milliseconds to0, floors seconds, uses seconds below60, unpadded m/s below1hour and h plus two-digit minutes thereafter. Without details the Loader output is unchanged (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/status-indicator.ts:40-130`).

Retry's initial seconds are ceil(delayMs/1000). CountdownTimer immediately invokes onTick with that value, then every1000ms decrements, ticks, requests a render, and at <=0 disposes and invokes onExpire. Even zero/negative initial durations wait for the first interval before expiry. It counts intervals rather than measuring a deadline, so delayed callbacks extend elapsed wall time. dispose clears the interval idempotently; Retry dispose clears both countdown and Loader. Retry text includes attempt/max and cancel-key hint. Retry/Compaction/BranchSummary setAppearance updates colors plus frame/interval options. Manual compaction says Compacting context; threshold says Auto-compacting; overflow prepends Context overflow detected. IdleStatus returns two space-filled rows at width (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/status-indicator.ts:132-258`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/countdown-timer.ts:1-40`).

The host replaces a status by cancelling any compaction hold, disposing the prior indicator and mounting the new one. Kind-filtered clear leaves a different indicator untouched; otherwise it disposes and clears, adding IdleStatus only after a prior indicator in regular mode with clearOnShrink. Successful compaction remains visible for at least1000ms from its shown timestamp, changing its label to Context compacted, then hands off to working only if still the same indicator and streaming/visible. The timeout has an identity check and is cancelled by replacement/clear. setWorkingVisible(false) clears only working; true while streaming can replace another current kind. Extension options are applied to an active working Loader directly (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:2873-2937`).

Preparing prompts skip registered extension slash commands, echo only plain parent-view prompts, and display an uninterruptible Preparing indicator showing the active extension path/event or Sending prompt. End preparation removes the echo and only clears its own still-active indicator. Working details add finalized output usage to ceil(current text+thinking+serialized tool-args JS length/4), explicitly flag the estimate, select the last pending tool's first title row at width200, and prioritize blocking child wait over tool detail over a rotating six-tip list (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:1524-1578`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:5462-5515`).

Compaction/retry events install and restore Escape handlers, set terminal progress, manage summary/error rows and hide transient retry-attempt errors. Summarization retries show retry then restore compaction/branch status per event source. SESSION owns the actual cancellation/retry state machine; this entry owns indicator mounting, feedback and timer lifetime. Tests assert elapsed formatting, detail rows, width30 clipping, frame updates and that dispose stops further render requests.
entries.interfaces: WorkingDetails{startedAt,outputTokens,outputTokensEstimated,thinking?,detail?,interruptible?}; StatusIndicator kind/dispose/setAppearance; WorkingStatusIndicator setDetails; RetryStatusIndicator(attempt,maxAttempts,delayMs); CompactionStatusReason manual|threshold|overflow. CountdownTimer(timeoutMs,tui|undefined,onTick,onExpire),dispose.
entries.dependency_text: Terminal Loader cadence/cancellation primitives are terminal-owned; SESSION-015–018 owns compaction/retry semantics and EXT owns working-indicator overrides. TUI owns their presentation and disposal.
entries.rust: Native StatusIndicator supports all four kinds, fixed themed spinner, elapsed time and a deadline-based retry countdown; it advances the spinner per render and emits one row rather than Loader's two-row shape. The fixed prefix is not clipped when width is smaller than it. It uses a literal Ctrl+C hint, lacks configurable appearance/frames and WorkingDetails, and its separate CountdownTimer has no callback/dispose thread to leak (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/status_indicator.rs:23-265`, `rust:crates/ice-tui/src/countdown_timer.rs:15-48`). Primary native working and compaction feedback is actually an editor WorkingState, gated by show_terminal_progress, rather than calls to the library working/compaction constructors. Native retry mounts StatusIndicator in the status container and is driven by the host render loop; remote TUI retry has its own retained slot. These working paths are credited, while TS detail/tip/estimate/hold contracts are absent (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/state.rs:987-1029`, `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/state.rs:1210-1239`, `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:1254-1282`, `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/tui_shell.rs:361-407`).
entries.port: Keep native deadline countdown and existing editor/status integration, then add typed working facts, configurable indicator appearance, real keybinding hints and explicit replacement lifetime. Separate terminal progress output from visibility policy where intended, and preserve successful compaction long enough to be seen without allowing stale timers to replace newer status.
entries.priority_reason: Native progress exists but lacks detailed live facts, configurable presentation and the exact operation handoff/visibility behavior.

entries.title: Subagent footer projection, resident counts, bounded activity and attention status
entries.what: Projects the live/historical agent view bridge into a compact footer with stable child identity, actual resident work/queue counts and advisory attention.
entries.mechanism:
The snapshot includes all non-parent views. Labels use role or label plus taskId or the first eight runId characters, replace C0/DEL controls with spaces, collapse spaces and clip to 128 cells. It takes the last three activities before filtering stale running activities from terminal views, then projects only bounded toolName (64 cells), optional path (96) and outcome. It freezes the outer snapshot, children, entries and activity projection; checkIn is retained by reference, so this is not a deep freeze of every nested supplied value. A displayed parent deliberately has no selected child fallback. Retained counts include reusable views; live attention includes finalization, defined repeat-failure count and due/queued/consumed/owner-unavailable check-ins (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/subagent-view-switcher.ts:60-199`).

Terminal statuses normalize underscores/hyphens, while a live finalization phase with absent/working control becomes FINALIZING. Advisory check-in state changes attention and detail text without replacing a working control state. The component subscribes to bridge events and replaces stale sampled view work counts with resident runtime-overview running/queued counts; liveCount remains the bridge count and only positive idle counts render. Elapsed time is supplied state, not advanced by a component timer. Dispose unsubscribes once (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/subagent-view-switcher.ts:113-148`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/subagent-view-switcher.ts:244-295`).

No children produces no rows. Width below 44 gives count-only text; 44–71 gives one identity/status row; at least 72 gives a second row only when selected-child detail exists. Detail includes outcome markers, safe activity, floored elapsed seconds, check-in status/ISO due time and repeat failures. Main view omits navigation hints; child view shows interrupt-to-main and previous/next bindings. Rows are cell-clipped/padded; customized appearance selects attention/running/muted presentation and may add a chrome border at width at least eight. Tests cover frozen bounded projections, terminal stale activity suppression, advisory owner-unavailable state, parent selection, overview precedence and 20/43/60/71/72/120-column output (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/subagent-view-switcher.ts:298-350`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/subagent-footer.test.ts:81-384`).
entries.interfaces: SubagentFooterActivity/Attention/Entry/Snapshot; createSubagentFooterSnapshot(views,selectedViewId,displayedId); formatAgentSwitcherLabel; SubagentFooterSwitcher.setAppearance,dispose,invalidate,render.
entries.dependency_text: SUB-016/036 own view lifetime, live/historical projection and input controls; SUB-037 owns the Hub. This entry owns the footer projection and presentation, not child execution or management.
entries.rust: The independently read native child host has plugin-owned jobs, cancellation, bounded text deltas and destructive polling that exposes running/done/failed and delays terminal results until queued deltas drain. Its state is not a live/historical view roster with retention, queue/attention/check-in projection (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/child_agents.rs:36-87`, `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/child_agents.rs:107-205`). A scoped crates search found no footer projection or matching attention/retention consumer. Native child execution and generic plugin UI remain valid capabilities; this specific built-in footer is absent. SUB-036 separately preserves the native side-question child path.
entries.port: Add the footer once the SUB view bridge is available, preserving bounded activity projection and overview-driven work counts. Keep check-in attention advisory and distinguish historical/reusable/live children. Define immutable ownership for nested check-in values and avoid implying elapsed time is freshly sampled without an event.
entries.priority_reason: Users need reliable child identity and attention without stale streaming flags or detailed action payloads leaking into the footer.

entries.what: Lists available palettes, previews selections, and switches the process-wide theme so interactive components and extensions see the same current palette.
entries.mechanism:
Available names combine the built-in catalog, valid custom JSON files and registered runtime themes, while the current palette is shared through a global symbol. Selection and preview update the live palette, with explicit dark fallback and error reporting when a load fails.

getAvailableThemesWithPaths first adds built-ins with their bundled JSON paths, then custom files under getCustomThemesDir, then registered themes with optional sourcePath; the first name wins in this listing, and final output sorts by name.localeCompare. Custom files are enumerated in Node readdir order, accept only a lowercase .json suffix, are individually parsed/constructed, and contribute the content name; errors are ignored here for the resource loader to report. getAvailableThemes returns names only. Runtime loading has a different precedence: registeredThemes.get(name) is returned first, then loadThemeJson. JSON loading itself prefers built-ins, then reads a registered sourcePath, rejects registered in-memory objects without a source path for export, then tries customDir/name.json. getThemeJsonData returns a structuredClone. getThemeByName suppresses any error and returns undefined. Consequently a content name differing from its custom filename is discoverable, but named loading needs the resource registry or a matching filename; the picker test proves discovery only (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:622-683`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:738-828`).

setRegisteredThemes clears the old Map and adds only truthy names, validating slash prohibition and letting later duplicate names replace earlier values. theme is a Proxy over globalThis[Symbol.for('@zykairotis/ice-coding-agent:theme')]; property access before initialization throws. This global object is shared by module loaders, while the registered Map/current name/watcher/callback are module state. The proxy returns the current property directly. initTheme chooses an explicit name or environment-derived default, loads it, optionally starts watching, and silently falls back to dark on error. setTheme records the requested name, loads, optionally starts watching and invokes the one registered onThemeChange callback; any error in that try block falls back to dark and returns success:false with a string message. A fallback load failure can still throw. enableWatcher:false does not explicitly stop an existing watch (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:983-1053`).

setThemeInstance installs the provided instance, sets current name to '<in-memory>', stops the watcher and invokes the callback; it has no local catch. onThemeChange replaces one callback rather than maintaining a subscriber collection. InteractiveThemeController.setThemeName and setThemeInstance disable automatic synchronization, apply the theme and call notifyChanged. applyThemeName records the requested name on success or dark on failure, invalidates the UI, invokes the supplied onChanged callback and optionally reports the load error plus dark fallback. preview resolves a setting/name against the current terminal theme, applies with watching, invalidates and requests render only on success; it does not replace activeThemeName or persist settings itself (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:1055-1066`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme-controller.ts:69-112`).

Extension-facing instance/name selection and name persistence are specified in EXT-049 (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/theme-selector.ts:5-67`).

entries.title: Per-tool render callbacks, row state and fallback rendering
entries.what: Allow a tool to render its call and result with persistent row state while preserving generic output when a renderer fails.
entries.mechanism:
Interactive tool rows can use independent call and result renderers supplied by the tool definition. They receive one shared state object for the row and a separate previous component for each render slot, so a plugin can update an existing display without losing execution state.

The component selects extension renderCall/renderResult individually, falling back to available built-in renderers and then generic formatting. renderShell defaults to the standard colored shell; self delegates framing to the returned component while host spacing and image handling remain. Render context includes current args, toolCallId, invalidate, lastComponent, state, cwd, executionStarted, argsComplete, isPartial, expanded, showImages and isError. invalidate clears cached rendering and requests a redraw; the state object survives subsequent updates. Result callbacks are actually passed {content,details}, plus {expanded,isPartial}; usage is not included in that supplied result object, and isError is supplied through context.

Callback exceptions fall back to generic tool rendering. The host appends image rendering rather than delegating all image handling to the plugin. Compact display uses separate previews: ordinary content is limited to five lines, edit/write preview to fourteen, running output to a three-line tail, and relevant error/bash branches choose their own head views; expansion requests the fuller renderer. Completed render output is cached by available width until invalidated. Registration alone causes no process execution, persistence or RPC callback evaluation. This contract is specific to transcript tool rows, not the custom message renderer registry.
entries.dependency_text: External services/binaries: none. Depends on the interactive transcript component/expansion contracts to be assigned by the TUI audit.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-plugin-sdk/src/lib.rs:348-353; rust:crates/ice-extensions/src/registry.rs:413-427; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/sessions.rs:425-610. Native tool schemas and executable registrations contain no call/result renderer callback, per-row plugin state, invalidation callback or render-shell choice. Native renderer kinds cover messages, entries and Markdown and do not implement a tool-row callback surface. JSON-rendered custom messages are therefore a related UI mechanism but cannot render an existing tool call through this contract.
entries.port: Define an owned, versioned tool-render request/response protocol in ice-plugin-sdk and route it through ice-tui's existing tool rows. Prefer declarative render output with explicit row state handles over foreign Component pointers. Give state and cached output runtime ownership, release them on row removal/reload, retain library keepalive across calls, and bound callback work. Implement call/result fallbacks and invalidation before enabling plugins to replace tool framing.

entries.title: Tool renderer composition, execution context, images and live result binding
entries.what: Combines built-in and extension call/result renderers, retains per-call rendering state across streamed arguments/results, and displays supported images without losing live completion bindings after transcript rebuilds.
entries.mechanism:
The component resolves the built-in tool definition for its cwd, then independently prefers the registered definition's renderCall, renderResult and renderShell properties. It retains argument, result, execution, expansion and image state and projects them into either a default boxed shell, a renderer-owned shell or the compact presentation described in TUI-032.

Options default showImages=true, imageWidthCells=60, compact=false and no toolsAppearance. Unknown tools have no built-in definition and use the default shell unless an extension requests self. The default tree has a leading Spacer1 and Box1/1 with pending background; call and result Component references are retained separately for renderer reuse. A shared mutable state object survives both renderers. Context includes args, toolCallId, invalidate, lastComponent, state, cwd, executionStarted, argsComplete, isPartial, expanded, showImages and isError; invalidate clears component/render caches and requests a UI render. isPartial initially true. markExecutionStarted and setArgsComplete update display, while argument/result setters retain new values and clear display caches. updateResult defaults isPartial=false and replaces the result rather than appending text (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/tool-execution.ts:40-238`).

Renderer exceptions fall back to generic call/result rendering. A result renderer receives content and details, with error state in context. The fallback call prints the tool name and JSON arguments; fallback results join textual blocks. Call and result renderer selection is independent, so a custom call renderer can retain built-in results and vice versa. Self shell omits generic box framing and can render no rows when its content is empty; it still uses the component's image children. Appearance affects state background/title/output styling but does not automatically impose all appearance-model geometry on an extension-owned component. Extension registration and transport remain EXT-owned.

Images are extracted from the latest result only when terminal image capability and showImages are true and both data/MIME exist. Each image gets maxWidthCells; the setter floors and clamps its value to at least1. Kitty skips non-PNG images until asynchronous convertToPng completes; converted entries are cached by image ordinal, followed by updateDisplay and requestRender. The ordinal cache is neither cleared when a different result arrives nor guarded by a result generation, and there is no in-flight deduplication in this component. Thus the source permits a prior or late conversion at the same ordinal to be reused for a later result. This is a TS state-lifetime limitation, not a contract to reproduce. Default/self shells include images when supported; compact rows include them only when expanded. Component rendering caches settled output by width, while partial output is recomputed, and setters/invalidate clear that cache (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/tool-execution.ts:243-285`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/tool-execution.ts:462-631`).

Interactive message_update creates missing tool components by ID and updates arguments on existing ones. Successful assistant message_end marks pending arguments complete; aborted/error completion turns all pending calls into error results and clears the map. tool_execution_start creates a missing component and marks execution started; updates replace partial result with isError=false; end applies the final error flag and removes the ID. Transcript reconstruction builds a temporary map, consumes matching historical results, and re-registers only unresolved calls into live pendingTools. The regression asserts that a subsequent live completion still updates a reconstructed call, and that completed history does not remain pending (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:4230-4343`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:4771-4816`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/suite/regressions/4167-thinking-toggle-pending-tool-render.test.ts:162-198`).

Tool component tests exercise partial arguments, renderer reuse/context, exception fallback, self shells, expansion, built-in resource/skill/doc read renderers and line-range labels. These source assertions were read, not executed. Actual read-tool resource recognition belongs to TOOLS; this entry owns composing those renderers into the transcript.

Running invalidates on each render; settled output is cached against width, component revision and theme revision. ToolPanel clamps horizontal padding to preserve a content column and clips/pads rows to the target width (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/tool_execution.rs:24-265`, `rust:crates/ice-tui/src/tool_execution.rs:361-626`, `rust:crates/ice-tui/src/tool_panel.rs:1-42`). Native host extension renderer routing is separately credited in EXT; its existence is not evidence that this component implements the TS context contract. Introduce generation-aware image conversion/cache ownership; maintain unresolved-ID bindings across rebuilds and explicit args-complete/start/partial/end phases.

entries.title: Compact tool rows, result precedence and bounded summaries
entries.what: Presents compact tool cells with state markers, operation-specific headers, bounded collapsed output and explicit expansion hints.
entries.mechanism:
Compact rendering separates a title from indented result rows and chooses preview content by a strict state/tool precedence. Completed rows are cached by width until component state changes; pending rows are recomputed, so streaming titles and partial output remain live.

Collapsed content width is capped at100 columns; expanded content uses the supplied width. A leading blank row is optional, title budget is max(1,width-2), and body budget max(1,width-4). The first body row uses two spaces plus the theme gutter and a space; continuation rows use four spaces. Body rows are clipped with a dim ellipsis, not wrapped by this layer. The first nonblank row and applicable more hints can carry the internal toggle URL (TUI-034). Fixed prefixes and max1 content budgets mean this layer does not establish a universal width invariant for widths below its indentation.

Edit with a string path uses Edit/Edit failed/Edited according to partial/error/success and includes added/removed counts when details.diff is a string. Diff counts count every leading '+'/'-' line. Bash with a nonblank command uses Running only when partial and executionStarted, otherwise Ran, including a call whose execution has not started. Collapsed command displays its first logical line plus an ellipsis when multiline; expanded displays the complete command wrapped by the header renderer. Other titles use renderCall output and fall back to toolName if it renders no lines. Path/title accents use global theme colors where coded, even when toolsAppearance supplies other text styles (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/tool-execution.ts:287-391`).

Collapsed-result precedence is: no result → no rows; partial → last3 normalized textual lines and a hidden-prefix hint; error → first5 error-styled lines plus more; successful edit with diff → rendered diff trimmed of blank ANSI rows and capped14; any own backgroundTaskId property in details → one summary line; a non-Bash result component → its rendered preview, capped14 for edit/write and5 otherwise; no textual lines → summarizer; other text → first3 dim lines plus more. Text joins text blocks, removes carriage returns and trims the end before splitting. An empty trailing-only output is distinct from missing result. The background preview branch tests property presence, whereas summarizeToolResult requires backgroundTaskId to be a string, so malformed metadata can fall through to a normal line-count summary. Expanded successful edits show the entire rendered diff without this height cap. Expanded non-edit calls use the full result renderer or styled raw text; edit errors or edits without a successful diff still take the collapsed body path even while expanded (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/tool-execution.ts:392-460`).

summarizeToolResult first recognizes a string backgroundTaskId and reports started vs moved to background according to origin. Next an edit diff produces literal added/removed counts; otherwise it returns textual line count, 'image' for empty text with an image block, or 'no output'. It does not execute or classify tool safety. Read description accepts nonblank path, appends offset and offset+limit-1 or1-limit when values are numbers, and imposes no finite/positive validation here; tool input validation belongs to TOOLS. grep/find and ls descriptions use their corresponding pattern/path fields. Tests assert pending/completed/error snapshots, partial tail behavior, diff counts, long commands, width100 capping, edit expansion and current theme colors (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/tool-summary.ts:96-146`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/compact-tool-rows.test.ts:1-228`).

entries.title: Exploration grouping and display-only shell summaries
entries.what: Groups adjacent read/search/list calls into one expandable exploration cell, while leaving execution and permission policy unchanged.
entries.mechanism:
createToolComponent groups a call only when tool style is compact, describeExploration returns a description, and the component does not render its own shell. entries.title: Compact tool rows, result precedence and bounded summaries
entries.what: Presents compact tool cells with state markers, operation-specific headers, bounded collapsed output and explicit expansion hints.
entries.mechanism:
Compact rendering separates a title from indented result rows and chooses preview content by a strict state/tool precedence. Completed rows are cached by width until component state changes; pending rows are recomputed, so streaming titles and partial output remain live.

Collapsed content width is capped at100 columns; expanded content uses the supplied width. A leading blank row is optional, title budget is max(1,width-2), and body budget max(1,width-4). The first body row uses two spaces plus the theme gutter and a space; continuation rows use four spaces. Body rows are clipped with a dim ellipsis, not wrapped by this layer. The first nonblank row and applicable more hints can carry the internal toggle URL (TUI-034). Fixed prefixes and max1 content budgets mean this layer does not establish a universal width invariant for widths below its indentation.

Edit with a string path uses Edit/Edit failed/Edited according to partial/error/success and includes added/removed counts when details.diff is a string. Diff counts count every leading '+'/'-' line. Bash with a nonblank command uses Running only when partial and executionStarted, otherwise Ran, including a call whose execution has not started. Collapsed command displays its first logical line plus an ellipsis when multiline; expanded displays the complete command wrapped by the header renderer. Other titles use renderCall output and fall back to toolName if it renders no lines. Path/title accents use global theme colors where coded, even when toolsAppearance supplies other text styles (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/tool-execution.ts:287-391`).

Collapsed-result precedence is: no result → no rows; partial → last3 normalized textual lines and a hidden-prefix hint; error → first5 error-styled lines plus more; successful edit with diff → rendered diff trimmed of blank ANSI rows and capped14; any own backgroundTaskId property in details → one summary line; a non-Bash result component → its rendered preview, capped14 for edit/write and5 otherwise; no textual lines → summarizer; other text → first3 dim lines plus more. Text joins text blocks, removes carriage returns and trims the end before splitting. An empty trailing-only output is distinct from missing result. The background preview branch tests property presence, whereas summarizeToolResult requires backgroundTaskId to be a string, so malformed metadata can fall through to a normal line-count summary. Expanded successful edits show the entire rendered diff without this height cap. Expanded non-edit calls use the full result renderer or styled raw text; edit errors or edits without a successful diff still take the collapsed body path even while expanded (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/tool-execution.ts:392-460`).

summarizeToolResult first recognizes a string backgroundTaskId and reports started vs moved to background according to origin. Next an edit diff produces literal added/removed counts; otherwise it returns textual line count, 'image' for empty text with an image block, or 'no output'. It does not execute or classify tool safety. Read description accepts nonblank path, appends offset and offset+limit-1 or1-limit when values are numbers, and imposes no finite/positive validation here; tool input validation belongs to TOOLS. grep/find and ls descriptions use their corresponding pattern/path fields. Tests assert pending/completed/error snapshots, partial tail behavior, diff counts, long commands, width100 capping, edit expansion and current theme colors (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/tool-summary.ts:96-146`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/compact-tool-rows.test.ts:1-228`).

Text results show first12 wrapped visual rows collapsed and all rows expanded. Diff rows are additionally capped6 collapsed and40 expanded, with fixed Ctrl+O hints. It does not implement the TS100-column compact layout, exact partial/error/edit/background/result-renderer precedence or per-tool3/5/14 limits (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/tool_execution.rs:361-536`). Its hand-written argument display parser has builtin path/pattern/command formatting and incomplete-JSON fallbacks, which are presentation-only rather than execution validation (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/tool_execution.rs:769-1177`). Make preview precedence explicit and independently test partial, failed, edit, background and renderer-owned results. entries.title: Application action links and incremental tool expansion
entries.what: Routes fullscreen transcript action links and expands tool output in newest-first batches, with per-cell overrides and shared group identity.
entries.mechanism:
The interactive composition root enables tool-toggle links only for fullscreen mode and supplies the fullscreen renderer an internal-action predicate plus URL callback. That callback first offers the URL to the application; a false result delegates to openBrowser. The main-screen renderer does not enable these click routes.

A process-global flag starts false. linkIceAction wraps text in OSC8 only when enabled; tool URLs are 'ice-action:toggle-tool/' plus encodeURIComponent(id). linkToolToggle copies the rendered row array and wraps only its first nonblank ANSI-stripped row, preserving the original array when disabled or empty. parseToolToggleUrl requires the exact prefix and catches malformed percent decoding; an empty suffix decodes to an empty ID. isIceActionUrl recognizes the broader 'ice-action:' prefix. More hints use current keybinding text, adding 'click or' only when links are enabled. Changing the global flag does not itself invalidate component caches (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/tool-toggle-link.ts:1-64`).

A ToolCell is a ToolExecutionComponent, ToolGroupComponent or a CustomMessageComponent with a toggle ID; other expandable cards are handled separately. The group ID is its first member, standalone tools use toolCallId and eligible custom completions use their custom toggle ID. toolExpandFrom is undefined for all collapsed, 'all' for all expanded, or a cell ID marking the first expanded tail cell. A missing anchor resolves to index0. Per-ID overrides take precedence over the tail rule. Each normal expand action moves the anchor backward3 cells, newest first; after reaching index0, the next action collapses everything. No cells still selects 'all' and emits the all-expanded status. A separate newest action toggles only the newest cell and reports 'No tool output yet' when absent. Explicit all-expanded/collapsed uses the same anchor mechanism. Changing the anchor clears overrides; when its overall boolean changes it also updates the active header and non-tool expandable children in loaded resources/chat. Applying cell expansion requests a render (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:5578-5654`).

handleUiAction recognizes exact bottom, shells, agents and prompt URLs; bottom scrolls to end, shells opens the shell view, agents opens the hub, and prompt scrolls to the sticky prompt target when available. A valid tool URL with an unknown ID is consumed without browser fallback. A known ID toggles its override and reapplies expansion. Unknown or malformed actions return false and therefore reach the URL opener configured at composition. The application does not implement an additional unknown-internal-URL rejection. Primitive hit testing, selection and hyperlink activation are TUI-224; this entry owns destination routing and state mutation (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:5656-5687`). Tests assert no links by default, title and more links for a standalone cell, and shared group links before/after expansion.
entries.interfaces: setToolToggleLinks(enabled),linkIceAction(text,url),linkToolToggle(lines,id),parseToolToggleUrl(url),isIceActionUrl(url),expandHint/clickOrKeyHint; createInteractiveTui(options.onAction). Tool expansion state is an anchor ID plus Map<string,boolean> overrides; TOOL_EXPAND_BATCH=3.
entries.dependency_text: TUI-224 owns the terminal's generic link hit testing/selection; later application entries own shell/agent/sticky-prompt view content. App keybinding registration depends on the terminal registry TUI-210.
entries.rust: Native primary CLI already binds TOOLS_EXPAND to toggle all tool outputs, persists display.tool_outputs_expanded as a session value, and requests rendering; it has no newest3 anchor or per-cell override behavior in that path (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:2282-2298`). Its mouse branch routes side-question mouse handling, scroll-to-end indicator, transcript wheel, Windows paste and selection/copy; it does not activate tool URLs there (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:1752-1850`). The native selection/scroll implementation is retained and assessed by TUI-223/224; absence of this application action dispatch does not mean mouse support is absent.
entries.port: Add stable transcript cell IDs, tail-anchor expansion and per-cell overrides on top of native expansion, then route internal actions before external URL opening. Retain native session persistence where useful and decide explicitly how unknown internal schemes are handled. Invalidate linked caches when switching renderers.
entries.priority_reason: Native global expansion works, but batch/newest expansion and clickable transcript actions are missing.

entries.title: User Bash streaming display, visual tail and completion presentation
entries.what: Shows user-invoked Bash progress and bounded visible output, including deferred placement, cancellation/exit notices and full-output references.
entries.mechanism:
The TS component creates a leading spacer, dim-or-Bash-colored dynamic borders, a command header and an animated Running loader with the current cancel-key hint. It accumulates incoming output deltas, then projects a context-limited tail into a20-visual-row collapsed preview or an expanded view.

appendOutput strips ANSI, normalizes CRLF and CR to LF, joins the first segment onto the previous last line and appends the remaining segments. The raw line array is not memory-capped here. updateDisplay calls the shared truncateTail with DEFAULT_MAX_LINES/DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES before presentation; expanded output therefore still excludes content removed by that context limit. Collapsed mode first keeps the last20 logical lines and then uses visual truncation at render width with a leading newline. Its hidden count is based on logical lines before the20-line slice, not all visual rows omitted by wrapping. Text rendering is cached per width until invalidate/rebuild. getOutput returns accumulated normalized output, not the displayed truncation (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/bash-execution.ts:95-163`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/bash-execution.ts:204-273`).

setComplete saves exitCode/cancelled/truncation/fullOutputPath, stops the loader and rebuilds. Cancelled takes status precedence; a defined nonzero exit code is error, while absent/null/zero is complete. Collapsed hidden output shows an expand hint; expanded shows collapse only when the logical hidden count was nonzero. Cancellation and nonzero-exit notices are separate lines. A full-output warning is emitted only when returned or local context truncation is true and a fullOutputPath is truthy. dispose stops the loader. The constructor uses dim command/borders when excluded from context, but updateDisplay uses Bash color for the header in the default appearance path, so exclusion's dim header is not retained after an update. Borders retain their initial color. Appearance replaces the border wrapper with applyChromeBorder and custom background/text/paddingX; the source does not automatically apply every stored appearance property (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/bash-execution.ts:32-94`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/bash-execution.ts:164-239`).

truncateToVisualLines renders Text(text,paddingX,0) at the requested width and takes the last maxLines rendered rows. Empty text returns zero rows; maxLines=0 is not specially handled in TS, so slice(-0) returns all rows while skipped reports the full length. Width and maxLines validation are not part of this helper. Native Text actually wraps, so the old native visual_truncate comment describing logical-line-only truncation is stale, not the runtime behavior (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/visual-truncate.ts:1-51`, `rust:crates/ice-tui/src/text.rs:78-94`).

The UI first emits the extension user_bash hook and reports hook failures without host-execution fallback. A hook's complete result is displayed and recorded directly. Otherwise it creates the panel, places it in pendingMessages when the session is streaming or chat when idle, feeds executeBash deltas through appendOutput, and applies completion metadata. Execution failure completes the panel with undefined exit and separately shows an error. The component reference is cleared afterward. Historical Bash messages restore saved output/exit/cancel/truncation/path; this branch does not apply global expansion before insertion (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:4625-4644`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:8128-8229`). Hook/session execution mechanics are EXT and TOOLS/SESSION-owned.

entries.dependency_text: TOOLS owns actual Bash process/capture/truncation semantics; EXT owns user_bash dispatch. TUI-205 supplies wrapping Text and the terminal worker owns Loader. This entry owns display accumulation/projection and the UI callback protocol.
entries.rust:
Native BashExecutionComponent already shows wrapped commands, state backgrounds, safe ToolPanel padding, elapsed duration, cancel/error and full-output notices,20-row visual tails and expanded output. append_output intentionally replaces a complete snapshot; the native primary caller passes get_progress().output snapshots, so the difference from TS delta accumulation is consistent, not a corruption bug (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/bash_execution.rs:23-416`, `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:559-630`). It normalizes tabs to4 spaces, has no independent context cap, uses a static running marker plus elapsed time, and preserves excluded command color. Expanded mode passes hidden=0, so its conditional collapse hint is not emitted; a truncation flag prints a full-output notice even without a nonempty path. Native visual_truncate explicitly returns empty for max_lines=0 and otherwise renders wrapping Text before slicing (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/visual_truncate.rs:1-108`). All native Bash inline tests were read through710.

A separate native transcript finalizer synthesizes exit_code as1/0 from is_error, forces cancelled=false and reads details.full_output_path plus details.truncation.truncated, so that event path does not preserve arbitrary exit codes/cancelled metadata even though the direct user-Bash caller does (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/transcript_view.rs:952-978`). This is scoped to that caller; process semantics are not inferred from UI flags.
entries.port: Preserve the native snapshot protocol and elapsed/width-safe rendering. Add the desired TS loader/key hints, appearance projection and context-limited preview semantics with clearly named delta vs snapshot methods. Carry real exit/cancel/path metadata through the generic transcript finalizer, and make expanded collapse hints and zero-line behavior explicit.

entries.title: Live model picker, favorites, scoped view and selection persistence
entries.what: Shows cached available models immediately, refreshes them with bounded cancellation, supports favorites and a scoped view, and applies the selected model to the current session.
entries.mechanism:
The component builds its border/title/search/list/details/hints synchronously from getAvailableSnapshot, requests a render, then begins a 15,000 ms refresh. It starts in scoped mode only when scopedModels is nonempty. Refreshed scoped entries are rebound through runtime.getModel(provider,id) when possible and retain their previous Model when unavailable. All-model ordering first prioritizes the current provider/id pair, then provider.localeCompare; a stable favorites-first pass subsequently places every favorite ahead of every nonfavorite, even the current model. Scoped ordering begins with configured order, with favorites affecting presentation only. Favorites are exact provider/id strings loaded into a Set (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/model-selector.ts:1-211`).

Search uses getModelSelectorSearchText: provider, provider/id, provider, id and optional name, with provider deliberately first for fuzzy scoring. The generic getModelSearchText used by the scoped editor starts with id instead. Nonempty filtering resets the selected index to zero; empty filtering clamps its prior index. Favorites-first sorting is applied after fuzzyFilter, so favorites can outrank a stronger fuzzy match. Toggle-favorite writes SettingsManager immediately, reapplies the filter and restores the selected model by identity. Toggling the scoped/all view is available only when scoped entries exist; changing favorites does not reorder the actual runtime scope. Up/down wrap, the favorite action is handled before Tab/view switching, and confirm/cancel are checked before passing data to Input (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/model-search.ts:1-22`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/model-selector.ts:212-406`).

The list renders at most ten rows centered around the selected index, using Text rather than single-line truncation. It marks current and favorite models, displays a scroll counter when needed and exposes the selected display name below. A catalog error replaces model details. Refresh shows muted progress, warning on timeout/abort or provider errors, and a success message otherwise. One provider error names that provider; multiple errors list provider keys. A closed selector ignores refresh completions; dispose is idempotent, clears the timer and aborts the controller. Filtering is reapplied after the refreshed snapshot, preserving the user's query but resetting a nonempty-query selection to its first result (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/model-selector.ts:103-340`).

Confirmation disposes the selector, persists defaultProvider/defaultModel, then invokes onSelect. The component does not await that callback. Its interactive caller awaits session.setModel, refreshes autocomplete/footer/border state, closes the selector, reports the selected model and invokes provider warnings/easter-egg checks. Failure closes the selector and reports the error; the already persisted default is not rolled back. This write-before-live-apply behavior is the observed TS contract, not an atomic operation (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/model-selector.ts:346-406`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:6472-6503`).

Read-only tests cover favorite ordering/toggling and selection retention, name/provider search, catalog errors and resetting filtered selection in both all/scoped modes. They were inspected, not executed. AUTH owns model resolution, refresh implementation and cycling; this entry owns picker state and its live-selection caller.
entries.interfaces: ModelSelectorComponent options include tui, currentModel?, settingsManager, modelRuntime, scopedModels:{model,thinkingLevel?}[], onSelect, onCancel and initialSearch?. Focus propagates to Input. dispose():void terminates owned refresh. getModelSearchText/getModelSelectorSearchText accept {id,provider,name?} and return their intentionally different fuzzy-search strings.
entries.dependency_text: Uses generic input/fuzzy/keybinding primitives and theme adapters. AUTH-024 owns scoped model matching and cycling; Settings owns persisted favorites/default fields. Session model transitions are SESSION-036.
entries.rust: The native live picker is present: model_selector_items deduplicates by API, lowercase provider and lowercase ID, emits provider-qualified values with display name fallback and provider-prefixed search text, and marks current by bare ID case-insensitively (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/settings.rs:530-575`). The live selector uses a snapshot, SearchableSelectList and ten-row SelectList; it does not explicitly preselect current, expose favorites/scoped mode, or run this owned refresh. It persists defaults only when the inferred current provider differs or is unknown, updates TuiState immediately, spawns lane.set_model while discarding its Result, reports success and closes before acknowledgement (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/selectors.rs:121-214`). `/model` uses the cached catalog for direct matching before opening the picker (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/commands.rs:117-174`). Native tests expressly cover qualified values, deduplication, provider/name search and ambiguous/package IDs (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/tests.rs:1816-1921`, `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/tests.rs:2468-2497`). Native catalog refresh elsewhere remains credited to AUTH; this is a caller-specific gap.
entries.port: Extend the existing native picker with identity-preserving cached/refresh state, favorites, scoped presentation and owned cancellation. Make live-apply failure and persistent-default sequencing explicit; matching TS write-before-apply is separate from a proposed transactional improvement. Preserve native qualified-ID/ambiguity handling and test the same-provider persistence difference.
entries.priority_reason: Model choice is a core interactive path; omitted refresh and differing acknowledgement/persistence can make visible state or future defaults diverge from the actual lane.

entries.title: Scoped-model editor, unavailable entries and session-only versus saved order
entries.what: Edits the ordered model scope used for cycling, preserves unavailable configured entries, and distinguishes immediate session changes from an explicit save.
entries.mechanism:
EnabledIds is null for all models or an explicit ordered string array. Toggling from null produces only the chosen ID; it does not disable one item from an implicit full set. Explicit toggle removes the first matching occurrence or appends. enableAll appends absent target IDs and collapses to null only when the resulting length and membership match allIds. clearAll from null returns allIds minus targeted IDs, or [] for an unfiltered clear. move swaps adjacent positions only in an explicit enabled array. getSortedIds places explicit enabled IDs, including unavailable IDs and retained duplicates, ahead of other catalog IDs. The catalog Map is last-wins by provider/id while allIds can retain duplicates (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/scoped-models-selector.ts:18-127`).

The component propagates focus to Input, uses eight centered rows, fuzzy-filters available entries by ID/provider/name and unavailable entries by full ID, and shows unavailable rows instead of discarding them. In null/all mode available rows omit checkmarks; explicit mode shows enabled/disabled marks, while unavailable rows always display unavailable/disabled presentation. The footer counts available enabled IDs separately from unavailable IDs, lists toggle/all/clear/provider/reorder/save hints and marks unsaved edits. updateModels preserves selected identity when it remains visible and optionally replaces enabledIds only when its second argument is supplied. A refresh-status Text is created only if the constructor received a truthy status; later setRefreshStatus is a no-op otherwise (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/scoped-models-selector.ts:129-279`).

Navigation wraps. Toggle, enable/clear filtered results, provider-wide toggle and reorder mutate session state through onChange with a cloned array/null. Mutating shortcuts mark dirty even when their helper returns an unchanged value. entries.what: Loads user and package JSON palettes, resolves reusable colors, and styles each semantic UI role while adapting hex colors to truecolor or a 256-color terminal.
entries.mechanism:
A theme file is validated before runtime construction, then every color variable is resolved and each foreground/background role is converted to an ANSI prefix. This allows the same JSON palette to work across terminal color capabilities while retaining separate colors for messages, tools, syntax and all thinking levels.

JSON parsing failures are wrapped as `Failed to parse theme <label>: <error>`. Runtime TypeBox validation requires string name and all 51 required color tokens; color values are strings or integers from 0 through 255. Missing required colors are accumulated, sorted, and reported separately from other instance-path errors. The explicit name assertion rejects any slash because slash separates automatic light/dark names. The published schema additionally declares a nonempty slash-free name pattern and additionalProperties:false at the top level, colors and export; the runtime schema construction does not explicitly include those options. Do not substitute published schema strictness for an unverified library default (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:26-107`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:685-751`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme-schema.json:12-15`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme-schema.json:309-342`).

Variable resolution returns numeric, empty or '#' prefixed values immediately. Other strings recursively index vars, fail with `Variable reference not found: <name>` when absent, and track visited names to fail with `Circular variable reference detected: <name>`. It does not interpret a '$' prefix. Before resolution, missing/nullish thinkingMax inherits thinkingXhigh; thinkingUltra inherits thinkingMax then thinkingXhigh; scrollbarThumb inherits selectedBg. Runtime Theme construction repeats the compatible optional-token fallbacks. Seven background keys are selectedBg, scrollbarThumb, userMessageBg, customMessageBg, toolPendingBg, toolSuccessBg and toolErrorBg; all other resolved keys become foreground colors (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:416-508`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:775-800`).

Color mode is an explicit argument or getCapabilities().trueColor ? truecolor : 256color. Empty strings yield SGR39/49 terminal defaults. Integers yield 38;5 or 48;5 without RGB conversion. A '#' string removes the first '#', requires six remaining characters, and parseInt-parses each two-character channel, rejecting only NaN channels; this is less strict than a full six-hex-digit regular expression. Truecolor emits 38;2;r;g;b or 48;2;r;g;b. The 256 approximation chooses each nearest cube channel from [0,95,135,175,215,255], preserving the earlier index on a tie; cube index is 16+36*rIndex+6*gIndex+bIndex. It also computes the nearest 24-step gray ramp (8+10*i), using rounded 0.299*r+0.587*g+0.114*b and weighted squared distance with those coefficients. Gray is selected only when maxChannel-minChannel<10 and its distance is strictly less than the cube distance. Theme.fg/bg fetch their precomputed map entry, throw for unknown tokens, and append only SGR39 or SGR49 respectively. A single theme name is fixed, while a setting with exactly one slash selects a light and a dark palette. The interactive controller queries terminal hints, falls back to environment evidence and keeps automatic settings synchronized with later terminal color-scheme notifications.

COLORFGBG detection splits semicolons and scans backward, parseInt-parsing each trimmed field until an integer0..255 is found; it can therefore skip an invalid trailing field. A notification is ignored unless automatic sync is enabled. entries.what: Chooses an initial palette from the terminal background and can follow terminal appearance changes using a paired lightTheme/darkTheme setting.

A single theme name is fixed, while a setting with exactly one slash selects a light and a dark palette. The interactive controller queries terminal hints, falls back to environment evidence and keeps automatic settings synchronized with later terminal color-scheme notifications.

With no setting it queries background at100ms, applies the detected palette, and persists/flushes only high-confidence detection; low-confidence fallback remains unpersisted. setThemeName/setThemeInstance disable automatic sync. rebindTui unsubscribes the previous callback, rebinds and restores the enabled notification state (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme-controller.ts:18-79`).

A notification is ignored unless automatic sync is enabled. Otherwise it updates terminalTheme, re-reads the current setting, disables sync if no longer a pair, and applies the selected side only when it differs from activeThemeName. Preview resolves against the recorded terminalTheme without itself changing automatic enablement. UI invalidation occurs through the controller's notifyChanged callback (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme-controller.ts:82-140`).
entries.interfaces: `TerminalTheme = "dark" | "light"`; detection DTO: `{theme,source:"terminal background"|"COLORFGBG"|"fallback",detail:string,confidence:"high"|"low"}`. Detector interface requires queryTerminalBackgroundColor({timeoutMs}):Promise<RgbColor|undefined> and optionally queryTerminalColorScheme({timeoutMs}):Promise<TerminalTheme|undefined>. Public helpers: parseAutoThemeSetting, resolveThemeSetting, getThemeForRgbColor, detectTerminalBackgroundFromEnv, detectTerminalBackgroundTheme, detectTerminalThemeForAuto, getDefaultTheme. Configuration is the existing theme string; automatic example is light-tokyo-night/dark-tokyo-night. Environment input: COLORFGBG.

entries.port: Add an interactive theme controller over existing theme state, terminal color queries and notification hooks. Preserve100ms query timeouts and confidence-based first-run persistence or document changed timing. Re-check the effective setting when notifications arrive, and detach/rebind listeners when terminal ownership changes. Ensure automatic changes invalidate component caches through the existing native revision mechanism.
